sourceEvidence.claim: The selectivity sentence (the 70S/80S rule)
sourceEvidence.quote:

ribosome (80S) unaffected.
All are bacteriostatic, except aminoglycosides (bactericidal) and linezolid (variable).

sourceEvidence.claim: The aminoglycosides card: MECHANISM (initiation complex, misreading, O2 for uptake)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM

Bactericidal; irreversible inhibition of initiation complex through binding of the 30S subunit. Can
cause misreading of mRNA. Also block translocation. Require O2 for uptake; therefore ineffective
against anaerobes.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The aminoglycosides card: CLINICAL USE + the Neomycin margin note
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Severe gram ⊝ rod infections. Synergistic with β-lactam antibiotics.
Neomycin for bowel surgery.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The aminoglycosides card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (myasthenia gravis, loop diuretics)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Nephrotoxicity, neuromuscular blockade (absolute contraindication with myasthenia gravis),
ototoxicity (especially with loop diuretics), teratogenicity.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The aminoglycosides card: MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE (acetylation, phosphorylation, adenylation)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE

Bacterial transferase enzymes inactivate the drug by acetylation, phosphorylation, or adenylation.

sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tetracyclines card: MECHANISM (aa-tRNA attachment, doxycycline fecal, the divalent-cation rule)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM

Bacteriostatic; bind to 30S and prevent attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA. Limited CNS penetration.
Doxycycline is fecally eliminated and can be used in patients with renal failure. Do not take
tetracyclines with milk (Ca2+), antacids (eg, Ca2+ or Mg2+), or iron-containing preparations
because divalent cations inhibit drugs’ absorption in the gut.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tetracyclines card: CLINICAL USE (intracellular accumulation, Rickettsia, Chlamydia, acne, community-acquired MRSA)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Borrelia burgdorferi, M pneumoniae. Drugs’ ability to accumulate intracellularly makes them very
effective against Rickettsia and Chlamydia. Also used to treat acne. Doxycycline effective against
community-acquired MRSA.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tetracyclines card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (with the source's own 'Teratocyclines' mnemonic)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

GI distress, discoloration of teeth and inhibition of bone growth in children, photosensitivity.
“Teratocyclines” are teratogenic; generally avoided in pregnancy and in children (except
doxycycline).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tetracyclines card: MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE (efflux pumps)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE

↓ uptake or ↑ efflux out of bacterial cells by plasmid-encoded transport pumps.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tigecycline card: heading + MECHANISM
sourceEvidence.quote:
Tigecycline
MECHANISM

Tetracycline derivative. Binds to 30S, inhibiting protein synthesis. Generally bacteriostatic.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tigecycline card: CLINICAL USE (MRSA, VRE)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Broad-spectrum anaerobic, gram ⊝, and gram ⊕ coverage. Multidrug-resistant organisms (eg,
MRSA, VRE).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The tigecycline card: ADVERSE EFFECTS
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Nausea, vomiting.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The chloramphenicol card: heading + MECHANISM (peptidyltransferase)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Chloramphenicol
MECHANISM

Blocks peptidyltransferase at 50S ribosomal subunit. Bacteriostatic.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The chloramphenicol card: CLINICAL USE (meningitis, RMSF, developing countries)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Meningitis (Haemophilus influenzae, Neisseria meningitidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae) and
rickettsial diseases (eg, Rocky Mountain spotted fever [Rickettsia rickettsii]).
Limited use due to toxicity but often still used in developing countries because of low cost.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The chloramphenicol card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (gray baby syndrome, UDP-glucuronosyltransferase)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Anemia (dose dependent), aplastic anemia (dose independent), gray baby syndrome (in premature
infants because they lack liver UDP-glucuronosyltransferase).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The chloramphenicol card: MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE (acetyltransferase)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE

Plasmid-encoded acetyltransferase inactivates the drug.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The clindamycin card: heading + MECHANISM (translocation)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Clindamycin
MECHANISM

Blocks peptide transfer (translocation) at 50S ribosomal subunit. Bacteriostatic.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The clindamycin card: CLINICAL USE (above the diaphragm vs metronidazole below)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Anaerobic infections (eg, Bacteroides spp., C perfringens) in aspiration pneumonia, lung abscesses,
and oral infections. Also effective against invasive group A streptococcal infection.
Treats anaerobic infections above the diaphragm vs metronidazole (anaerobic infections below
diaphragm).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The clindamycin card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (pseudomembranous colitis)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Pseudomembranous colitis (C difficile overgrowth), fever, diarrhea.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The linezolid card: heading + MECHANISM (23S rRNA, initiation complex)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Linezolid
MECHANISM

Inhibits protein synthesis by binding to the 23S rRNA of the 50S ribosomal subunit and preventing
formation of the initiation complex.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The linezolid card: CLINICAL USE (MRSA and VRE)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Gram ⊕ species including MRSA and VRE.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The linezolid card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (myelosuppression, serotonin syndrome, partial MAO)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Myelosuppression (especially thrombocytopenia), peripheral neuropathy, serotonin syndrome (due
to partial MAO inhibition).
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The linezolid card: MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE (rRNA point mutation)
sourceEvidence.quote:

Point mutation of ribosomal RNA.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The macrolides card: heading + drug line
sourceEvidence.quote:
Macrolides

Azithromycin, clarithromycin, erythromycin.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The macrolides card: MECHANISM (the source's own 'macroslides' gloss)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM

Inhibit protein synthesis by blocking translocation (“macroslides”); bind to the 50S ribosomal
subunit. Bacteriostatic.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The macrolides card: CLINICAL USE (atypicals, STIs, B pertussis)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Atypical pneumonias (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Legionella), STIs (Chlamydia), gram ⊕ cocci
(streptococcal infections in patients allergic to penicillin), and B pertussis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The macrolides card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (the source's own MACRO mnemonic set + P-450)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

MACRO: Gastrointestinal Motility issues, Arrhythmia caused by prolonged QT interval, acute
Cholestatic hepatitis, Rash, eOsinophilia. Increases serum concentration of theophylline, oral
anticoagulants. Clarithromycin and erythromycin inhibit cytochrome P-450.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The macrolides card: MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE (23S methylation)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM OF RESISTANCE

Methylation of 23S rRNA-binding site prevents binding of drug.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The polymyxins card: heading + drug line (colistin, polymyxin B)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Polymyxins

Colistin (polymyxin E), polymyxin B.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The polymyxins card: MECHANISM (cation polypeptides; the C1-prefixed arrows the normalizer strips)
sourceEvidence.quote:
MECHANISM

Cation polypeptides that bind to phospholipids on cell membrane of gram ⊝ bacteria. Disrupt cell
membrane integrity →  leakage of cellular components →  cell death.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The polymyxins card: CLINICAL USE (salvage therapy, triple antibiotic ointment)
sourceEvidence.quote:
CLINICAL USE

Salvage therapy for multidrug-resistant gram ⊝ bacteria (eg, P aeruginosa, E coli, K pneumoniae).
Polymyxin B is a component of a triple antibiotic ointment used for superficial skin infections.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The polymyxins card: ADVERSE EFFECTS (neurotoxicity, respiratory failure)
sourceEvidence.quote:
ADVERSE EFFECTS

Nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity (eg, slurred speech, weakness, paresthesias), respiratory failure.
